questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Achieve better english speaking skills and explore a foreign university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a benefit for me to live on campus, as I was with other students a lot of the time, which meant that I talked more english than if I had lived in the city centre by myself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite stressful at times, because we got all the information about the modules and arrivals in the beginning of September, while we already had to leave for the exchange in mid-september, so it was hard to plan anything before last minute.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did get e-mails about arrival and there where webinars about the academic life at Kent.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It would have been helpful to get a studentadvisor attached earlier.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were different types of housing, e.g. self-catered and part-catered, but most of them were quite expensive.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in self-catered, where there was a nice kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is worth noting that you need to buy all utensils, plates, cups etc., as there is nothing in the house, when you move in. This was inconvenient for me, as I only stayed for 3 months, but had to buy everything anyway.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration happened quite late (around august/start sep), which meant that everything was quite a rush at the time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to e-mail the Erasmus office, but e-mails often take 2-3 days, sometimes more to be answered, so a lot of things were slowed down by this process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get the modules that I wanted, one module was already full, while there was one module, that I did not get offered, but it was available to me, which I was quite disappointed about as the module was just in my interests.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise future students to ask the univeristy which modules are available for short term students, that have to take the exams in the end of the term, as this means a lot as to which modules you will be able to undertake.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the courses were quite interesting and had relevant themes, but it bothered me that there were not more seminar hours than 1 seminar hour per. week per. module.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much more focus on discussion and philosophical issues about the area of law.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Environmental law, critical and legal reasoning, asylum and refugee law and privacy and data protection

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Asylum law and privacy were really great courses.
I learnt a lot from critical and legal reasoning as well and the teacher in environmental law was really committed to the course, which made the seminars really good.

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I expected the accommodation to be a lot cheaper, than it turned out to be.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of different societies and I really benefitted from joining as you get to talk to other students more easily.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything - cultural, sports, arts...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The mountaineering society was really great and had a lot of nice trips and socials as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend doing the hike along the cliffs of Dover and going to London, Cambridge and Oxford.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the societies

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The part about living with other students and the fact that the supermarket at campus was always empty

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There were always a lot of social gatherings after doing sports at the societies, which was really great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join a society, live on campus and buy cheap kitchenware.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Its worth noting that the campus accommodation is really expensive and that there are few seminar/lecture hours at law.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning better english and getting to know a lot of nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That all the books were online, so it was a lot of reading on a computer, which was tiring. It was also very challenging to read so many academic texts in English.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
